[MUQATIL:12:91-95/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The brothers admit wrongdoing and say God chose Joseph over them; Muqatil links “we will not choose you” in 20:72 to this sense of choosing. | mentions 20:72
[MAJAZ:v1p317/r2] MAJAZ, d. 209 · author | holds | وإن كنا لخاطئين means وإن كنا خاطئين; the added fatḥa-lām intensifies and confirms, and خطئت and أخطأت are equivalent.
[MAJAZ:v1p317/r3] MAJAZ, d. 209 · امرؤ القيس | reports | Imruʾ al-Qays uses خطئن to mean أخطأن.
[MAJAZ:v1p317/r4] MAJAZ, d. 209 · أمية بن الأسكر | reports | Umayya ibn al-Askar’s line uses خطئا and حابا in the same sense of error.
[TAB-FULL:v13p329/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Joseph’s brothers say God preferred him over them, granting him knowledge, forbearance, and virtue.
[TAB-FULL:v13p329/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The brothers admit they wronged Joseph by separating him from his father and brother and through their other mistreatment.
[TAB-FULL:v13p329/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | خطئين means mistaken; the source distinguishes خطئَ يخطأ from أخطأ يخطئ and cites Umayya al-Askar’s verse as usage evidence.
[TAB-FULL:v13p329/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · السدي | reports | The brothers apologize to Joseph for what they had done to him after he identifies himself. | mentions 12:90
[TAB-FULL:v13p329/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · قتادة | reports | After Joseph identified himself, the brothers recognized that God had made him a forbearing man.
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2194/r1] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · قتادة | reports | Qatadah says the brothers admitted God had favored Joseph over them and that they had encountered a forbearing man.
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2194/r2] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · ابن إسحاق | reports | Ibn Ishaq glosses أثرَك as God having favored Joseph over them.
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2194/r3] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · ابن إسحاق | reports | Ibn Ishaq says the brothers meant that they had done wrong in what they had done to Joseph.
[NAHHAS:v2p343/r3] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | آثرك means preferred you; its active participle is مؤثر and verbal noun إيثار; خطئين means committing error.
[THALABI:v5p254/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | خاطئين means guilty or sinful; the source gives its verb forms and cites Umayya's verse as evidence.
[THALABI:v5p254/r2] THALABI, d. 427 · أمية بن الأكسر | reports | Umayya's line uses خطئا to mean they sinned.
[THALABI:v5p254/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says they missed the truth even though they acted intentionally; every sinner leaves the path of truth for doubt and disobedience.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r1] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | The brothers' admission that they were at fault refers to what they did to Joseph; it can mean either sinful or mistaken, with sinful implying culpability.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r2] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | Although the brothers were young when they first acted, they became culpable by growing up and continuing to conceal what they had done.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p76/r9] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Joseph accepted hardship for God over bodily pleasure, and God later favored him over his brothers. | mentions 12:91
[QUSHAYRI:v2p90/r11] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The brothers swear that God favored Joseph, reversing their earlier denial of his merit; one who truly witnesses does not deny.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الأصمعي | reports | آثرتك means I preferred you; أثير describes someone specially favored and given preference.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الليث | reports | An athīr is someone whom another favors with special virtue and connection.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | He glosses the confession as God having preferred Joseph over the brothers.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · المفسرون | reports | They specify Joseph's advantages as knowledge, forbearance, intelligence, virtue, beauty, and kingship.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس وغيره | reports | Ibn Abbas glosses خاطئين as sinners; another reported gloss says they sinned against Joseph, meaning they were nothing but wrongdoers.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r6] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن الأنباري والزجاج | reports | خاطئين may mean مخطئين; al-Zajjaj chooses this sense, supported by the poetic use خطئن meaning أخطأن.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r7] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The lexical distinction between خطئ and أخطأ was discussed at the verses about sin and inadvertent error. | mentions 2:81, 2:286
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:90-93/r3] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | The brothers acknowledge that God favored Joseph over them with intellect, knowledge, excellence, and beauty, and they admit their wrongdoing.
[JISHUMI:v5p3709/r10] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | إيثار means preferring one thing over another and relates to choice and the lasting good impression behind أثر, آثار, and مأثرة.
[JISHUMI:v5p3709/r11] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | A خطيئة is moving something from its proper course; خطئ is deliberate misplacement, unlike أخطأ, which means to err or sin.
[JISHUMI:v5p3710/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | خاطئين is accusative as the predicate of كان.
[JISHUMI:v5p3710/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Joseph's brothers say God chose and favored him over them in knowledge, judgment, and kingship.
[JISHUMI:v5p3710/r4] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو علي | reports | One explanation says they were mistaken in concealing Joseph's affair from their father.
[JISHUMI:v5p3710/r5] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | Other glosses take خاطئين to mean sinners generally or wrongdoers against one another.
[JISHUMI:v5p3710/r6] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو علي | reports | Abu Ali says the brothers began the wrongdoing in childhood but reached adulthood still concealing it from their father.
[JISHUMI:v5p3710/r7] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | Other explanations say they had to seek forgiveness after puberty, or that repentance was commendable though not obligatory and thus Joseph prayed for it.
[JISHUMI:v5p3710/r8] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | A further view says they were already adults but not prophets; the author prefers the view that they began as children and continued the concealment into adulthood.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p274#2/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The brothers apologize, acknowledging that God preferred Joseph and that their treatment of him was sinful; khatiʾ is deliberate error, while akhtaʾ is inadvertent error.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The brothers’ confession that God preferred Joseph is a plea for reconciliation and implicitly admits their guilt; athara covers all forms of preference and gifts.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Khāṭiʾūn means those who intentionally commit error, unlike mukhṭiʾ, one who aims correctly but misses; Umayya ibn al-Askar supplies a poetic example.
[TABRISI:12:90-92#2/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The brothers admit they sinned and say God favored Yusuf with patience, knowledge, reason, beauty, and kingship; their admission shows remorse rather than persistence.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الضحاك عن ابن عباس | reports | The brothers say God preferred Joseph in kingship.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · أبو صالح عن ابن عباس | reports | They say God preferred Joseph for his patience.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · أبو سليمان الدمشقي | reports | They say God preferred Joseph for his forbearance and forgiveness toward them.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | A fourth interpretation includes Joseph’s knowledge, intelligence, beauty, and the other virtues he was given.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | The brothers admit they were sinners and guilty regarding Joseph.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r6] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن الأنباري | reports | Khāṭiʾīn was chosen over mukhṭiʾīn because the former means sinful, while the latter means merely missing the right course without sin.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r7] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن الأنباري | reports | The form khāṭiʾīn may also have been chosen to match the verse endings.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r8] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | Al-Farraʾ gives two senses for in: “although we were sinners” or “we were only sinners.”
[RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الأصمعي | reports | Al-Asmaʿi explains “ātharaka” as God favoring Joseph; the phrase can also describe a servant whom someone prefers with special gifts.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Joseph was favored over his brothers in knowledge, forbearance, reason, virtue, beauty, and kingship.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Some infer that Joseph’s brothers were not prophets: prophethood outweighs worldly offices, so sharing that rank would make their confession of his superiority incoherent.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | “Khāṭiʾ” denotes deliberate sin, unlike “mukhṭiʾ,” used for someone who strives to reach a legal judgment but errs.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Most commentators say the brothers apologize for throwing Joseph in the well, selling him, and separating him from their father.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · أبو علي الجبائي | reports | Al-Jubbaʾi says they did not apologize for childhood acts before puberty, but for later hiding Joseph’s survival and failing to tell Jacob that the wolf had not eaten him.
[RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | rejects | Razi rejects al-Jubbaʾi’s account as implausible: Jacob would hardly send unaccompanied prepubescent boys; even an unnecessary apology can still be fitting, as people may renew repentance after forgiveness.
[QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The

 hamza in ātharaka is lightened rather than fully realized; the verb means God preferred Joseph and chose him for knowledge, forbearance, judgment, intellect, and kingship.
[QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | Asked how the brothers could call themselves sinners despite acting deliberately, Ibn ʿAbbās answers that they knowingly acted but first missed the truth and departed its proper path.
[QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Their admission of wrongdoing carries an implicit request for pardon; every sinner has left the path of truth and fallen into doubt and disobedience.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:12:91/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The brothers acknowledge that God chose Joseph over them for his good appearance and complete conduct.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:12:91/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | They admit that their conduct toward Joseph made them sinners.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#3/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | They acknowledge that God preferred Joseph over them through knowledge, forbearance, piety, patience, and beauty.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#3/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Their confession means they had deliberately sinned, neither practicing piety nor patience.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#3/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Joseph's kingship and their abasement as suppliants before him are the consequences of their wrongdoing.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p316/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Īthār broadly means favor and all kinds of gifts.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says God favored Joseph with kingship, patience, and knowledge.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو سليمان الدمشقي | reports | Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi says God favored Joseph with forbearance and forgiveness.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari relates God’s favor to piety, patience, and the conduct of the good, matching the preceding verse.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The brothers’ confession that Joseph was favored also seeks to elicit his kindness and acknowledges their wrong.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Khāṭiʾīn describes deliberate wrongdoing, whereas akhṭaʾ describes aiming at what is right but failing to attain it.
[SAMIN-DURR:12:91/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | آثرك means ‘favored you’; إيثار is preferring someone in all kinds of gifts, from أثر, following a thing as though tracing every kind of honor.
[SAMIN-DURR:12:91/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The hadith ستكون بعدي أثرة means that some people will monopolize goods over others; استأثر means to reserve something for oneself, and God's استأثر بفلان figuratively means He chose him.
[SAMIN-DURR:12:91/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشاعر | reports | An unnamed poet's line uses آثرك الله به إيثاراكا to attest God's granting special preference.
[BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The Joseph story teaches patience, measured action, and entrusting matters to the Wise; difficult affairs unfold gradually as causes are ordered, testing both obedience and disobedience. | mentions 12:110
[BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The brothers confess God preferred Joseph over them through knowledge, intellect, judgment, beauty, rule, piety, and other virtues; the shortened “in” heightens their urgent apology.
[BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | They call themselves intrinsically wrongdoers; “khaṭiʾīn” denotes deliberately committing sin.
[DURR-FULL:v4p577/r6] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · قتادة | reports | Qatadah says Joseph proved gentle: he did not expose or rebuke his brothers for their past acts.
[ITQAN:v2p499/r1] ITQAN, d. 911 · author | holds | The non-governing lām of initiation emphasizes a clause and shifts away from sentence-initial position after inna to avoid two successive emphatics; it also makes the imperfect refer to the present.
[ITQAN:v2p499/r4] ITQAN, d. 911 · author | holds | The lām of an oath’s response, or of law and lawla, appears in the examples cited; the target verse’s لقد آثرك الله is an oath response. | mentions 21:57, 48:25, 2:251
[ITQAN:v4p328/r1] ITQAN, d. 911 · البارزي | reports | Al-Barizi says eloquence chooses the most fitting words for each part of a sentence; humans cannot usually summon every meaning and matching expression, while this is present in God’s knowledge, making the Quran the finest and most eloquent speech.
[ITQAN:v4p328/r6] ITQAN, d. 911 · البارزي | reports | Al-Barizi illustrates preference for lighter diction with آمن over صدق, آثرك الله over فضلك, أتى over أعطى, أنذر over خوف, خير لكم over أفضل لكم, and shorter nominal forms and تنكح.
[BURSEVI:v4p204/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | reports | After recognizing Joseph, the brothers approach the throne intending to fall at his feet; he descends and embraces them.
[BURSEVI:v4p204/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The brothers admit God favored Joseph in beauty, perfection, status, and wealth, and say they knowingly committed sin.
[ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | prefers | Alusi prefers that God's favor meant the brothers were surpassed through piety and patience; other reports explain it by kingship, patience and knowledge, forbearance, or a wider list of virtues and royal power.
[ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · سليمان الدمشقي | reports | Sulayman al-Dimashqi explains God's favor as Joseph's forbearance and forgiveness.
[ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · صاحب الغنيان | reports | The author of al-Ghunyān lists Joseph's good character and appearance, knowledge, forbearance, beneficence, kingship, patience with their harm, and power as reasons for God's favor.
[ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The brothers admit they were deliberate sinners; the circumstantial conjunction marks their state, إِنّ is lightened with an implicit pronoun of شأن, and the lām in the predicate is the shifted emphatic lām.
[ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Calling themselves intentional sinners both seeks Joseph's kindness and confesses their wrongdoing with an implicit signal of repentance.
[ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | خاطئين derives from a verb for intentional sin, unlike أخطأ, which describes aiming at what is right but failing to attain it.
[TABATABAI:12:89-92/r5] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Ithar means choosing or preferring, and khatiʾ and mukhtiʾ both denote one who errs; the brothers acknowledge their wrongdoing and God’s preference for Joseph.
[ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them. | mentions 2:216
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-surah-maryam-19:p194/r5] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The brothers' admission recognizes that their resentment came from their father's preference for Joseph, while God's preference exposed their error and affirmed Joseph's deserving status.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r1] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Joseph identifies himself by recalling what his brothers did to him and Benjamin, fulfilling the revelation that he would later tell them of it when they did not recognize him (12:15). | mentions 12:15
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r2] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | His brothers admit their wrong and apologize, and Joseph tells them he forgives them.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r3] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Envy cannot block a blessing God has decreed; the Prophet prayed that no one can withhold what God gives, and the brothers ultimately acknowledge God favored Joseph over them.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r4] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · Resûlullah | reports | The Prophet’s prayer says no one can prevent what God grants, and no one can grant what God withholds.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r5] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · Ziyâ Paşa | reports | Ziya Pasha’s couplet says divine power eventually makes tyrants admit that God favored another over them.
[QIRAAT-ER:12:91:13#1/r1] QIRAAT-ER · author | holds | A dialectal or Quranic variant simplifies and drops hamza in khāṭiʾīna, without changing meaning.
[SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p638/r1] SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT · author | holds | Tāʾ is an oath particle restricted to the name Allah; it occurs five times in the Qur’an, three in Joseph and twice in al-Naḥl. | mentions 12:73, 12:85, 16:56, 16:63
[SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p638/r2] SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT · author | holds | Tāʾ in this oath conveys veneration and is etymologically a substitution for wāw, which is commonly used to swear by other things such as dawn, forenoon, night, and sun.
[SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r2] SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT · author | holds | Joseph’s brothers did not ask him to forgive them or name their offense, using a light إن; to their father they explicitly requested forgiveness and admitted their sins emphatically with إنّا. | mentions 12:98
[STUDYQURAN:12:91/r1] STUDYQURAN · Kl | reports | Joseph’s no-reproach statement is called a beautiful form of forgiveness; reproach may also mean physical punishment.
[STUDYQURAN:12:91/r2] STUDYQURAN · Prophet Muhammad | reports | At the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet cited Joseph’s forgiveness, then freed Quraysh after they acknowledged his noble status.
